summary.headline: Tata Steel 1QFY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, up Rs 2,400/t YoY, with India at Rs 19,162/t despite Rs 1,200 crore West Asia cost hit.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 60,794 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, with consolidated EBITDA per ton tracking near Rs 13,000 (about 15% margin). India EBITDA rose 32% YoY to about Rs 9,900 crore, but India volumes were hit by shutdowns and snags (crude 5.76 Mt, deliveries 5.17 Mt). Netherlands was weighed down by the Direct Sheet Plant shutdown since April and a chrome-emission issue, while UK losses narrowed to -£27 million. Management guided India realisations down about Rs 1,500/t in 2Q and flagged regulatory risk in the Netherlands that may make the DRI-EAF transition conditional.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Crude steel 5.76 Mt and deliveries 5.17 Mt in 1Q, with realisations up about Rs 5,990/t QoQ; costs rose about Rs 6,700/t from lower volumes and snags. Management expects 2Q realisations about Rs 1,500/t lower than 1Q, with 2Q rupee EBITDA better on higher volume.

segments.name: Automotive & Speciality
segments.commentary: Best-ever 1Q volumes and 21% YoY growth in high-end sales; new DP980 cold-rolled UHSS for commercial vehicles and galvannealed grades for passenger vehicles. Company cites about 50% share in the auto sector.

segments.name: Downstream and branded products
segments.commentary: Tata Tiscon volumes up 33% YoY; Tata Steelium up 34% YoY on Kalinganagar cold rolling mill. Digital platforms Aashiyana and DigECA combined GMV about Rs 2,200 crore, up 61% YoY. Tubes and tinplate posted their strongest 1Q ever.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Deliveries 0.5 Mt; realisations up about £91/t QoQ, costs up about £54/t, EBITDA up about £36/t. A 3 June Port Talbot pickle line fire cut volumes by about 10,000 t and EBITDA by about £5 million in 1Q.

segments.name: Netherlands (TSN)
segments.commentary: Liquid steel 1.55 Mt and deliveries 1.4 Mt. Direct Sheet Plant (about 1.4 Mtpa, about 20% of output) shut since early April, and chrome-emission exceedance hit almost the full quarter; costs rose €118/t vs revenue up €87/t.

guidance_outlook: India NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower in 2Q vs 1Q, with long products hit harder by monsoon construction slowdown; flat products supported by auto demand.
2Q coking coal consumption cost: India about $5/t higher, Netherlands about $10/t higher, with coking coal at about $184/t.
UK realisations guided up another £70-80/t in 2Q; substrate costs will absorb part of the gain. UK EBITDA breakeven guided for 2H FY27, possibly slipping to 3Q or 4Q.
Netherlands NSR guided about €10/t higher in 2Q (after about €70/t in 1Q vs €80/t guided); management expects 2Q volumes and EBITDA better than 1Q.
Consolidated cost headwind of about Rs 1,200 crore from West Asia war in 1Q, expected to taper in coming quarters.
Depreciation to rise by about Rs 300 crore per quarter (about Rs 1,200 crore a year) from accelerated amortisation of mining and PPE assets ahead of 2030 mine re-auction.
NINL 4.8 Mtpa expansion approved at Rs 33,873 crore; zero date 1 August 2026, 48-month commissioning timeline. NINL merger with Tata Steel expected by end of FY27.
UK 3 Mtpa EAF site works, equipment sourcing largely on schedule; National Grid high-voltage connection delay acknowledged.
capex_capacity: NINL 4.8 Mtpa long-products expansion (wire rods and rebars) approved at Rs 33,873 crore, taking site to 6.2 Mtpa in phase 1 and toward 10 Mtpa overall; MKB iron ore mine expansion of 15 Mtpa in phases, outside this capex.
Kalinganagar phase 2 (5 Mtpa) and Ludhiana 0.75 Mtpa EAF (about Rs 3,000 crore, built in two years) are ramping up.

0.5 Mtpa combi mill at Jamshedpur commissioned and midway through ramp-up; 0.3 Mtpa tinplate and 0.74 Mtpa hot-roll pickling and galvanising expansions due within 30 months; about 0.42 Mt of tube capacity to be added in FY27 via asset-light model.
Netherlands DSP restart: four-week extended trial starting about 5 August; remediation of chrome emission issue reportedly completed.
Maharashtra greenfield now planned at about 15 Mtpa in three 5 Mtpa blast furnaces (earlier 6 Mtpa); land about 3,000+ acres; engineering not yet started.
demand_pricing: Europe: prices stuck around €700/t and demand weak; inventories above average. Management expects gradual, phased increases from the November contract season as EU quotas fall to 18 Mt of 30 Mt import volume and CBAM applies.
UK: tariff-free quotas cut by about 3.3-3.4 Mt effective 1 July, with 50% duty above quota; management wants quotas by product category, citing galvanised steel and tubes at 70-80% of demand.
European prices closing on US prices; the gap has narrowed to about $300-400/t versus $100-200/t historically (per management).
India: auto demand strong; long products (construction) weaker during monsoon. Tata Tiscon volumes up 33% YoY.
Shipbuilding approvals received (Lloyd's, ABS and others); about 100 kt targeted this year, potentially 0.5 Mt. Data-centre steel and storage solutions being pursued in India and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will EU restocking and the quota/CBAM changes drive a significant European price uptick, given prices have stayed near €700/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an uptick from the November contract renegotiation season as 18 Mt of 30 Mt imports are removed by quotas, but increases will be phased rather than sharp.

qa_highlights.question: Is UK EBITDA breakeven in 2H still achievable given the safeguard outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the goal is unchanged, possibly slipping from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q, with the November contract round as the signal of price stickiness.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Maharashtra capex now 5 Mt rather than 6 Mt, and why is NINL capex about 33% higher per tonne than Kalinganagar?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra now targets about 15 Mtpa in 5 Mtpa blast furnaces for productivity; NINL is treated as greenfield given enabling works and layout, plus exchange-rate effects on imported equipment.

qa_highlights.question: Captive iron ore plans post-2030 and whether 50% captive still holds at 40 Mtpa?
qa_highlights.answer: Current output about 45-50 Mt, 90% from old mines; newer mines (under 5 Mt) to reach 30-35 Mt. Management will judge captive versus market ore on economics, since ore at 120-140% premium makes imports an option.

qa_highlights.question: Netherlands: does DRI-EAF avoid the chrome and coke-oven issues, and is the company still keen on the Netherlands?
qa_highlights.answer: DSP issue relates to tunnel-furnace rollers and is said to be addressed; the wider DRI-EAF investment is under reassessment given slag and regulatory conditions, with a decision dependent on regulation, CBAM, quotas and returns.

qa_highlights.question: NINL commissioning timeline and Ludhiana EAF economics?
qa_highlights.answer: NINL 48 months from 1 August 2026. Ludhiana relies on local scrap within 300 km and saves about Rs 3,000-4,000/t in logistics; full-year numbers expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining assets revert for re-auction in 2030 with right of first refusal, so depreciation is accelerated by about Rs 300 crore a quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Up about Rs 2,400/t YoY and about Rs 1,490/t QoQ on per-ton basis
EBITDA margin 26-27%, up about 95 bps QoQ
From -£48 million in 4Q; fourth straight quarter of improvement

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / net debt to EBITDA

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 45,950 crore, incl. Rs 13,221 crore cash

risks_watch: Netherlands regulatory risk: DSP restart on about 5 August is a four-week trial; continued operation beyond that depends on regulator approval, and management is reassessing whether the DRI-EAF investment is viable given slag, CBAM, quota and EU ETS conditions.

UK EBITDA breakeven timing: management says it may slip from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q, with the November contract round as the test of whether price increases stick; UK quota allocations for galvanised steel and tubes are still under negotiation.
India 2Q margin compression: NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower QoQ, with long products weaker in monsoon; management expects rupee EBITDA better on higher volumes.
European prices remain stuck near €700/t with above-average inventories; recovery is expected to be phased from the November contract season, not sharp.
Iron ore cost path post-2030: captive mix (about 50%) and the 30-35 Mt target from newer mines depend on premiums of 120-140%; management did not quantify the blended cost increase.
Execution: NINL 4.8 Mtpa (zero date 1 August 2026, 48 months), UK EAF power connection delay from National Grid, and Port Talbot pickle line ramp-up to normal levels by 3Q/4Q.
key_quotes: So, our hypothesis was fundamentally based on the initial proposals that were given. We still believe, as we see, that the prices have increased and there are certain segments of value -added products like galvani sed or tubes in UK
It may be pushed by one quarter and may not be in 2Q but 3Q or 4Q. In the second half, we should be able to be closer to breakeven.

So, we are looking at it from that perspective. The next phase beyond Neelachal will be of course, there is an opportunity in the next three years to build a couple of more EAFs like the one in Ludhiana.

So, in a nutshell, you can say that we are currently reassessing the situation with all stakeholders to understand the investability of the DRI – EAF, the regulatory framework within which there is not just an investment case but also a sustenance case
India capital allocation story is not dependent on Europe. It will follow its own course, and it will continue to grow in both upstream and downstream.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India operations, pricing and downstream growth, with management stating that the India capital allocation story is independent of Europe. Noticeably cautious and guarded on the Netherlands (regulatory conflict, DRI-EAF under reassessment) and on UK breakeven timing, which management said may slip by one or more quarters.
